why: Rule 1 fully satisfied at the only real cluster: 15002 is the deg-2 junction between two Bragg ends (52.8 cm muon rising 53k->128k into 15000, 9.1 cm proton stub hot at 15003), and the zoom shows both attached segments as green arrows.

Rule 7 apex: in X-Z the whole 342 cm shower opens as a clean V whose apex is 23009 at the lowest z (426 cm), with two ~24 cm prongs getting hotter away and a 2.1 cm 151k e/cm recoil stub sitting on the apex itself; downgraded from certain because the prongs could be hadronic (rule 4).

Rule 1 textbook: 3 of 4 segments rise away from 3011 - a 190 cm muon with a clean template-following Bragg at 3000, a 28.7 cm proton rising monotonically 35k->230k into 3007, and a pion that stops at 3004 where it makes a secondary star of short hot stubs.

The event is a single 15.7 cm flat-MIP segment with no dQ/dx gradient at either end, so the only real discriminator is that the 18000 end sits at y=-198.0 against the -200 wall and must be an exit/entry, leaving 18001 as the only end that can be an origin.

Classic two-Bragg-ends trap resolved by rule 1: both prongs rise away from the deg-2 junction 3002 (46.3 cm arm climbing the muon template to 210k at 3001, 17.7 cm arm reaching 240k at 3000), so 3002 is the point they both point away from.

12003 is the deg-2 junction where an 89 cm muon leaves and Braggs at 12001 while a 7 cm proton stub Braggs at its free end 12000; only 1 of 2 formally rises away and the muon carries a hot spike at the 12003 end itself, so the junction wins but less cleanly than the other two-prong events.

Rule 8 abstention: cluster 6 is a single 21 cm curled MIP squiggle with no Bragg anywhere and both free ends (6006, 6000) reading red/flat, and its only apex-like point - the 6005/6003 hairpin - lies at y=199.4 against the 200 cm top wall, so there is no contained origin to name.

Rule 1 with both prongs measured: from 6002 a 104 cm muon runs flat at MIP and Braggs to 125k at 6001 while a 36.1 cm proton falls monotonically from 330k at 6000 back to 90k at 6002, so both stop away from 6002.

All three attached segments show green arrows at the deg-3 junction 3004 - a 6.3 cm stub climbing 39k->110k into 3001, a 5.8 cm prong rising to 79k at 3005, and a 19 cm MIP track running off to 3003 - the complete everything-comes-out-of-the-vertex signature.
Both arms of the 90 cm cluster Bragg away from the deg-2 junction 18002: a 45.2 cm proton on the proton template reaching 220k at 18000 and a 44.3 cm muon flat at MIP then rising to 205k at 18001.
